title: Chatstream probabilistic concurrency fabric for tokenflow benchmarking
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Objective: Build a repeatable, templated load fabric that simulates realistic multi-tenant streaming chat/completions traffic over SSE and WebSocket protocols, optimized for long-run tokens/sec measurement, robust p95 tracking, and automated regression detection. This ticket covers the harness implementation, telemetry contract, CI integration for perf gating, and a first full-run baseline against the current runtime-1.18 configuration.

Why: Existing drivers focus on short bursts or deterministic session types. Production traffic is probabilistic: varied prompt lengths, token emission shapes, KV-cache warm/cold mixes, session churn, and mixed-tenancy interference. We need a fabric that can express that uncertainty, produce stable time-series (tokens/sec, connect success, p95 chunk latency), and detect regressions automatically when model/runtime changes are rolled out.

Goals:
- Achieve reproducible tokens/sec runs that exercise prefix caching and cold-paths (goal: 25M tokens/sec sustained on our dedicated staging pool at nominal capacity).
- Provide p95 and p99 chunk-latency reporting for both first-byte and tail-chunk times per session.
- Implement automated regression detection rules and integrate with perf CI (Slack alerts + GitHub check).
- Emit standardized telemetry events and aggregated stats to our perf S3 bucket and the Grafana dashboard.

Out of scope: full UI for job composition (will be follow-up), on-prem installation packaging (handled by Private infra team).
acceptance_criteria:
- Fabric can run SSE and WebSocket client families concurrently against a given endpoint URL.
- Run config supports: tenant mix (N tenants), prompt length distribution, token emission distribution (burst vs steady), KV-cache warm ratio, reconnect/churn model, and session affinity policies.
- Metrics emitted at 1s resolution: tokens/sec (global & per-tenant), success rate, connection churn, p50/p95/p99 first-byte and last-chunk latencies, token drop/retransmit counts.
- Regression detector triggers a GitHub check failure when p95-first-byte increases >10% vs baseline across 3 consecutive runs or when tokens/sec drops >12% sustained for 5m.
- Baseline run artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/streaming/baselines/ENG-275998/ with run metadata and raw event logs.
- Dashboard panel with heatmap and cohort comparison for quick triage.
run_plan:
Generator model: probabilistic session generator with 4 persona classes (short chat, multi-turn assistant, long completion, streaming narration).
Message length distributions: short: 8-32 tokens, medium: 64-256, long: 512-2048 (Pareto tail).
Token emission profiles: immediate-burst (most completions), steady-stream (streaming narration with 20-40 tps), and token-drip (very low tps to simulate slow connections).
KV-cache mix: warm (70%), lukewarm (20%), cold (10%) per-session; backend will include a KV warmup path to toggle stateful cache hits.
Session lifecycle: connect -> initial prompt -> 0-6 followups -> reconnect probability per session 7%.
Connection churn: configurable churn curve (sine + Poisson jitter) to stress admission.
Concurrency targets: run templates for small (10k concurrent sessions), medium (100k), and stress (500k) across regions.
Measurement windows: 15m steady-state window after ramp for core metrics.
telemetry_contract:
Edge counters and histograms we will emit:
- perf.tokens.emitted (counter, labels: run_id, tenant, persona)
- perf.session.connects (counter, labels: result:ok|err, proto:sse|ws)
- perf.chunk.latency (histogram ms, labels: first_chunk|any_chunk, tenant, proto)
- perf.kvcache.hit (counter, labels: warm|lukewarm|cold)
- perf.stream.errors (counter, labels: type:timeout|broken_pipe|protocol)
- perf.tokens.rate (gauge rps sampled 1s)
Artifact paths: raw events -> s3://redwood-perf/streaming/runs/{run_id}/events.ndjson, aggregated -> s3://redwood-perf/streaming/runs/{run_id}/summary.json
regression_detection:
Algorithm: hybrid rules + statistical control.
Baseline: rolling median of last 5 nominal baselines per config.
Primary gate: p95(first_chunk) increase >10% vs baseline AND absolute increase >25ms for 3 consecutive CI runs -> FAIL.
Secondary gate: tokens/sec decline >12% sustained over 5 minute steady window -> WARN -> escalate if persists for 15 minutes.
Anomaly detector: EWMA on p95 with alpha=0.2 to pick up drifts, and two-sided 3-sigma outlier detection for single-run spikes.
When triggered: collect full raw event dump, run differential trace between baseline and current (bucketed by persona), post link in GitHub check with contextual slices (tenant, region, kv-cache status).
observability_integration:
Prometheus exporter embedded in driver (endpoint /metrics). Metric prefixes as in telemetry_contract.
Grafana: dashboard ID perf-streaming-ENG-275998 (staging org). Panels: tokens/sec (global/tenant), p95 first-chunk by persona, heatmap of per-session tail latencies, connection churn timeline, KV-hit ratio trend.
Alerts: Slack channel #perf-regressions, with run artifacts and links to dashboard. GitHub checks via perf-ci-bot that can block runtime-1.19 merges.
implementation_notes:
Driver is Go-based (reuse existing multiplex client library). Key components: session generator, protocol adapters (SSE, WSS), telemetry sink, run coordinator, and result uploader.
We will containerize the runner and use k8s job templates to scale horizontally; runner shards will write to local buffered files and a collector aggregates to S3.
Performance considerations: minimize per-connection goroutine cost by using pooled encoders and non-blocking sockets; use samplers to limit raw event uploads at high scale (full raw logs only for failing runs).
Security: runner should not ship secrets; endpoint auth via ephemeral tokens provisioned by perf infra.
progress_updates: 2025-02-16: spike meeting w/ infra and runtime team. Agreed on metric names and baseline path. Decided to land minimal proto for sse adapter by 2/21.
2025-02-21: prototype SSE client committed (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-driver/pull/412). Basic streaming with first-chunk timing works locally.
2025-02-25: added persona generator and KV-cache toggles. Started synthetic run on small staging pool; observed unexpected token emission rate variance due to backpressure behavior.
2025-02-27: implemented EWMA-based drift detector and basic GitHub check integration. CI job created but currently gated from blocking merges until we tune sensitivity.

2025-03-02: first medium run (100k sessions) completed; tokens/sec stable but p95-first-chunk elevated by ~18% in eu-west compared to us-west. Collector uploaded artifacts to s3://redwood-perf/streaming/runs/2025-03-02-ENG-275998/
2025-03-03: triage with runtime team: root cause likely scheduling differences on the eu-west staging pool; created follow-up ENG-276010 to tune kernel selection heuristics.
next_steps:
- Stabilize websocket adapter and run a 3-run baseline across regions (target dates 3/6-3/9).
- Tune regression thresholds after 3 baselines and enable GitHub check gating for patch branches.
- Add tenant isolation experiments to quantify noisy-neighbor effects.
- Document run templates and provide one-click job YAML examples for Perf and Release engineers.
